scale.Confirmed: Announced by the company or shown in an official source.
scale.Likely: Multiple credible outlets or hard evidence (certifications, databases, supply chain), but no official word.
scale.Rumor: One or few sources, an estimate, or a leaker claim. Plausible but unverified.
scale.Shaky: Weak sourcing, conflicting reports, a bad track record, or a guess presented as news.
scale.Debunked: Contradicted by the company or by clear evidence.

items.title: Apple launches OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros and an M6 lineup at its Oct 28 launch
items.expected: Oct 28, 2026 (Apple 'Pro and tell'); on sale Nov 6 (reported)
items.claim: At its Oct 28 launch Apple will announce OLED touchscreen 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros (M5 Pro/Max), an OLED iPad mini, a 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro and an M6 iMac, with sales from Nov 6.
items.why: The date is now official: on Oct 19 Apple's Greg Joswiak posted the invite for a 'Pro and tell' media experience in Los Angeles on Oct 28 at 10 a.m. PT, one day after Bloomberg's 'on or around Oct 27'. The tagline points to the MacBook Pro, but Apple has not named any product, so the line-up remains a Bloomberg report. Supporting evidence: Bloomberg called the Oct 13 launch correctly; an unreleased iPad mini Smart Folio (A3632) appeared on Apple's French regulatory site; and Gurman says Apple Stores plan an overnight reset on Nov 5-6. The chip question has largely settled: Gurman, 9to5Mac and MacRumors now all say the OLED models use the existing M5 Pro/Max, with M6 only in the entry 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac. Update Oct 26: part of the claim is already confirmed. Apple announced the OLED iPad mini (8.5-inch, A20 Pro) by press release, with pre-orders Oct 28 and availability Nov 6, matching the reported Nov 6 sales date. Greg Joswiak then teased an 'exciting week', and Gurman's Oct 25 newsletter repeats that the touchscreen MacBook Pros come Wednesday. The MacBook Pro and iMac parts are still unannounced. We will resolve this on Oct 28. Update Oct 27: more of the claim is now confirmed, a day early. Apple announced the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 ($1,999) and the iMac with M6 ($1,499) by press release, both with pre-orders Oct 28 and availability Nov 6, matching Gurman's line-up and the Nov 6 sales date. Only the OLED touchscreen 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros remain unannounced; Gurman still expects them Wednesday. We keep this at Likely and will resolve it on Oct 28.

sources.name: Apple Newsroom (14-inch MacBook Pro with M6)

items.title: Standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e arrive in spring 2027
items.claim: Apple is splitting its iPhone releases: Pro and foldable models in fall, the standard iPhone 18 and 18e in spring.
items.why: Reported repeatedly by Mark Gurman and echoed by several outlets. The fall 2026 lineup (iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo) matched the split. Apple has not confirmed the spring models or date.

items.title: Galaxy S27 family has four models, including a compact S27 Pro
items.claim: Samsung will release the Galaxy S27, S27+, S27 Pro and S27 Ultra.
items.why: Model numbers for all four (SM-S952U, SM-S956U, SM-S958U and a global dual-SIM SM-S957B/DS) appeared in the GSMA IMEI database, which is strong evidence a phone exists but does not confirm names, specs or launch dates. On Oct 16, two more model numbers (SM-S9570 and SM-S9580, believed to be the Pro and Ultra) appeared in China's MIIT certification database. On Oct 20 leaked third-party screen protectors showed only the S27, S27+ and S27 Ultra (6.27, 6.66 and 6.89 inches), without the Pro. Accessory leaks are less reliable than certification databases, so we keep this at Likely for now. On Oct 22-23, batteries for the S27 Pro (EB-BS957CBY) and S27 Ultra (EB-BS958DBY) passed Safety Korea certification, another regulatory sign that a Pro model exists.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Unpacked lands around Feb 24, 2027
items.claim: Samsung will hold its Galaxy S27 Unpacked in late February 2027, possibly on Feb 24.
items.why: This is an estimate extrapolated from past schedules (Jan 17, 2024; Jan 22, 2025; Feb 25, 2026) and early One UI 9.5 firmware testing, not a leak from Samsung. Samsung usually sends invitations about two weeks before the show. Re-rated Shaky on Oct 19: Korean tipster Lanzuk, who has a solid Samsung record, now says Samsung is aiming for early January 2027, which contradicts the late-February guess.

items.title: Galaxy S27 parts ramp to mass production in mid-October
items.claim: Some Galaxy S27 components entered mass production in September, with all four models ramping in mid-October.
items.why: Single-source report from ZDNet Korea relayed by SammyGuru and iDevice. Samsung has not commented.

items.title: NVIDIA RTX 50 Super cards debut at CES 2027
items.claim: NVIDIA will launch the RTX 5060 Super (12GB), 5070 Super (18GB) and 5070 Ti/5080 Super (24GB) around CES 2027.
items.why: Earlier reports named CES 2027, but a later September 2026 report says NVIDIA has no RTX 50 Super plans for 2027 and the refresh may not ship. The dates have moved repeatedly and the sources conflict. On Oct 12 Taiwan's BenchLife reported a 24GB RTX 5080 for Q1 2027 that would replace the 16GB card; it is unclear whether that is the rumored 5080 Super or a different plan (tracked separately below).

items.title: NVIDIA RTX 60 series slips to 2028
items.claim: The next GeForce generation will miss 2027 and reach retail in 2028; AMD will have only one RDNA 5 GPU in 2027.
items.why: Based on a leaker's claims reported by Club386 and a Verge report that the lineup could miss 2027. Neither company has confirmed. On Oct 12 the same leaker, Kepler_L2, said AMD is unlikely to even announce RDNA 5 before Computex (June) 2027 and that a later 2027 reveal is more likely. AMD has published no schedule.

items.title: Intel Nova Lake-S desktop CPUs debut at CES 2027
items.claim: Intel will launch Core Ultra 400 'Nova Lake-S' desktop chips at CES 2027, with first retail models in Q1 2027.
items.why: Several outlets report a CES 2027 debut and Q4 2026 mass production. The origin is leakers and supply-chain reports, and Intel has not confirmed a date.

items.title: AMD Zen 6 desktop chips show up at CES 2027
items.claim: AMD's Zen 6 'Olympic Ridge' desktop CPUs will be revealed at CES 2027 with retail from March to June 2027.
items.why: Trade-press reports of a delay from earlier plans; retail window is an estimate. AMD has not confirmed.

items.title: OpenAI's first device is a screenless smart speaker with a camera
items.claim: The first Jony Ive-designed OpenAI device is a hockey-puck-sized speaker with a camera and sensors, priced around $200-$300.
items.why: Form factor and price come from reports and leaks that OpenAI has not confirmed. One piece is firm: a court filing says no shipping before the end of February 2027.

items.title: Apple unveils smart glasses at WWDC 2027
items.claim: Apple will show privacy-focused smart glasses at WWDC 2027 and ship them in late 2027.
items.why: Reporting traces back mainly to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who also warns it could slip to late 2028 or 2029. The camera design decision was reported as not final.

items.title: PS6 and the next Xbox slip because of the memory shortage
items.claim: Sony's PS6 and Microsoft's next Xbox (Project Helix) will launch later than planned because of high memory prices.
items.why: Sony's CEO said the PS6 launch date is still undecided because of the component shortage, and Microsoft's new CEO admitted the next Xbox is affected. The 2028-2029 timeframe for PS6 is a report, not a statement. On Oct 20 Fortune reported, citing people familiar with Microsoft's plans, that the Project Helix console is planned for 2028, with a next-gen Xbox handheld possibly by the end of 2027; see our separate price rumor.

items.title: Tesla unveils Optimus V3 before the end of 2026
items.claim: Tesla will publicly show its Optimus V3 humanoid robot in 2026.
items.why: Elon Musk had targeted a July-August window that passed without a reveal. On the Oct 21 Q3 earnings call Tesla said early production of Optimus had begun on its Fremont line, but it did not present a new version, and Musk promised only a video 'within a month or two' showing unscripted tasks, with deliveries to outside companies around the end of 2027. Treat Tesla timelines with caution.

items.title: Microsoft's next Xbox console costs $1,200-1,800 and launches in 2028
items.claim: Microsoft's Project Helix console will cost between $1,200 and $1,800 unless Microsoft subsidizes it, and will launch in 2028, with a next-generation Xbox handheld by the end of 2027.
items.why: One report, from Fortune, based on unnamed sources; GameSpot, Engadget and Ars Technica relayed it. The price is a projected range that depends on whether Microsoft eats some of the cost, and memory shortages make high prices plausible. Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet disputed the same story's account of the handheld's software, though not the price or timing. Microsoft has announced no date or price.

items.title: OnePlus readies a Turbo Pro phone with an unreleased Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Pro
items.claim: OnePlus is developing a Turbo Pro (possibly Turbo 7 Pro) with a new 3nm Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Pro (SM8845 Pro), a 6.78-inch 1.5K 185Hz screen, a 200MP main camera and a 9,000mAh battery, launching around the end of the year.
items.why: From Digital Chat Station, a prolific Weibo tipster with a decent record, in a post he later edited; Android Authority reported it. Qualcomm has not announced a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Pro, and OnePlus has not mentioned the phone. The timing is vague. GSMArena adds that the tipster also mentioned a clip-on external fan accessory, and that the screen, camera and battery match the OnePlus 16; the same SM8845 Pro chip is rumored for the iQOO Z12 Turbo/iQOO 16R.

items.title: NVIDIA's RTX 6060 doesn't arrive until 2029
items.claim: NVIDIA's budget RTX 6060 will launch around 2029, well after the higher-end RTX 60 cards, and may not match the PS6's gaming performance.
items.why: Leaker Kepler posted this in a NeoGAF thread, and TechRadar relayed it via Wccftech. He framed it as a guess based on NVIDIA's past habit of delaying low-end cards during shortages, not as inside information. It assumes the RTX 60 series itself lands in 2028, which is also only a rumor (see our RTX 60 entry).

items.title: Honor Win 2 and Win 2 RT launch in October
items.claim: Honor's Win 2 and Win 2 RT phones launch this month with 100W/90W charging and 10,000mAh+ batteries.
items.why: Honor announced on Oct 12 that the Win 2 series would launch Oct 21, and it did: the Win 2 arrived in China with a 10,100mAh battery and 100W wired charging, so the battery and 100W parts of the claim held up. Honor launched the Win RT 2 and Win Turbo 2 alongside it, but we could not verify the 90W charging figure the original leak gave for the other models.
items.outcome: Confirmed: the Win 2 launched in China on Oct 21 with a 10,100mAh battery and 100W charging. The 90W claim for other models is unverified.

items.title: OPPO Find X10 launches worldwide on Oct 21
items.claim: OPPO's Find X10 goes on sale on Oct 21.
items.why: We first rated this Shaky because the only clue was a UK promotion ending Oct 21. OPPO then confirmed an Oct 21 global launch, and on the day it published prices and opened orders in Europe (Finland: EUR 1,499 and EUR 1,799). But 'on sale' only partly held: European deliveries start Nov 2, Singapore pre-orders open Oct 22 with deliveries from Oct 26, and India launches Oct 22.
items.outcome: Mostly confirmed: launched and orderable on Oct 21, but phones ship from Nov 2 in Europe, so it was not in buyers' hands that day.

items.title: Claude 6 arrives around May 2027 and GPT-7 around Jul-Aug 2027
items.claim: Anthropic's next flagship lands around May 2027 and OpenAI's around July-August 2027.
items.why: These are prediction-market and blog forecasts. Neither company has announced model names or dates.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra may switch to Exynos 2700 because Snapdragon overheats
items.claim: Samsung found the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheating in S27 Ultra testing and may use its own Exynos 2700 chip if Qualcomm doesn't fix it by mid-October.
items.why: The report came from Korean outlet SEDaily and was relayed by SamMobile and others. Qualcomm told 9to5Google on Oct 17 the overheating reports are 'inaccurate', and its CMO Don McGuire says there are 'no systemic thermal issues'. A separate Oct 16 MoneyToday report says Samsung has dropped the Exynos plan for the Ultra because of Exynos supply limits and memory costs, and the Ultra will use Snapdragon only. Samsung has not commented. Single-sourced, denied, and now contradicted by another report. An Oct 19 Lanzuk leak (via SamMobile) also says the Ultra may use Qualcomm's chip exclusively.

items.title: Galaxy S27+ drops ultra-wideband (UWB)
items.claim: The Galaxy S27+ may lose UWB, a feature Samsung has offered for years.
items.why: Leaker Abhishek Yadav found two S27 models (SM-S9570 and SM-S9580, believed to be the Pro and Ultra) in China's MIIT certification database with UWB listed, and says the S27 and S27+ lack it; SammyFans reported precise tracking may be Pro/Ultra-only. The certification is real evidence for the two higher models, but the S27+ losing UWB is an inference from what is missing. Samsung has not commented.

items.title: Apple Intelligence fully launches in China with iOS 27.3 in December
items.claim: After an October beta, Apple will roll out Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3 in December, without the new Siri, Image Playground or the newer Genmoji.
items.why: Reported by Bloomberg. The groundwork is confirmed: Tim Cook said on Oct 15 that a beta arrives this month after regulators approved the first features and Alibaba's Qwen models, and the SCMP reports China's MIIT granted network permits for the models. Apple has not given a date or feature list for the full launch.

items.title: One UI 10 is Samsung's biggest software overhaul yet
items.claim: Samsung's One UI 10 will be its biggest software overhaul yet, built around cross-app 'contextual flow', fewer menus and tighter device handoffs, possibly with paid tiers for heavy AI features.
items.why: Comes from an unnamed insider via Nokia Power User, relayed by GSMArena; tipster Ice Universe, who has a solid Samsung track record, says his own source confirms 'significant changes, unprecedented in nature'. Timing is disputed: SamMobile expects mid-2027 with the Galaxy Z Fold 9 and Flip 9, while GSMArena's reading of the insider points to the Galaxy S29. Samsung has said nothing, and the details are vague.

items.title: GTA VI comes to PC in Q1 2027
items.claim: Rockstar plans to release the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI in the first quarter of 2027, a few months after the Nov 19 console launch.
items.why: GamesBeat reports this from four anonymous industry sources; The Verge, Polygon and others relayed it, but nobody has independent confirmation. Rockstar did not comment, and its store page still lists only PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It would be a much shorter gap than GTA V's 19-month wait for PC.

items.title: NVIDIA swaps the RTX 5080 to 24GB in Q1 2027
items.claim: NVIDIA will release an RTX 5080 with 24GB of GDDR7 in early 2027, gradually replacing the 16GB model.
items.why: Single-source report from Taiwan's BenchLife, relayed by VideoCardz and TechPowerUp. Board partners reportedly have only verbal guidance and no design documents yet, so timing is soft. Technically easy: 3GB memory chips on the same 256-bit bus. NVIDIA has not commented. Comes amid tight RTX 5090 supply, which NVIDIA says is constrained but not discontinued.

items.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra gets thinner bezels and a thicker camera bump
items.claim: The Galaxy S27 Ultra will have 1.28mm screen bezels (vs 1.32mm on the S26 Ultra) and a 4.69mm camera bump, slightly thicker than today's.
items.why: Measurements come from leaker Ice Universe, who has a good Samsung record, relayed by SamMobile. They fit separate case leaks showing a wide camera bar on the Pro and Ultra. Small, unverified numbers; Samsung has said nothing.

items.title: OnePlus Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro both get 200MP main cameras
items.claim: Both OnePlus Ace 7 models will use a 200MP main camera, and the Pro adds a 50MP 3.5x periscope.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, relayed by GSMArena. OnePlus has now set the launch for Oct 29 and confirmed the chips (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 'V series' for the Ace 7, standard 8 Elite Gen 5 for the Pro) and the cooling fan, and on Oct 26 it confirmed the Pro half of the claim: a 200MP main camera plus a 3.5x periscope telephoto on the Ace 7 Pro (it did not state the periscope's resolution). The standard Ace 7's camera is still unconfirmed. We will resolve this at launch.

items.title: Galaxy S27 series launches in early January 2027
items.claim: Samsung plans to launch the Galaxy S27, S27+, S27 Pro and S27 Ultra in early January 2027, a few weeks earlier than the S25 and S26.
items.why: From Korean tipster Lanzuk on Naver, who has a solid track record on Samsung, relayed by SamMobile and GSMArena. The leak says major hardware is finalized but Samsung is still deciding whether the Pro and Ultra get LPDDR6 and UFS 5.0 because of memory prices. GSMArena reads it more loosely as a return to the usual January-February window. Samsung has not announced anything.

items.title: PlayStation 6 costs $1,000 or more
items.claim: Memory and storage alone will cost Sony about $680 per PS6, pushing the console's price to $1,000 or more.
items.why: Leaker KeplerL2, who has a decent hardware track record, made the $680 claim on NeoGAF and earlier estimated a $960 bill of materials (in July). The $1,000 price is an inference from those cost estimates plus Sony saying it does not intend to sell hardware at significant losses, not a leaked price. Sony has not said when the PS6 launches or what it costs.

items.title: vivo X500 Ultra uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a huge battery and a bigger 200MP telephoto
items.claim: The vivo X500 Ultra launches in China around March-April 2027 with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a flat 6.85-inch BOE LTPO screen, an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor, a 7,000-8,000mAh battery, a 50MP Sony LYT910 35mm main camera and a 200MP 1/1.2-inch telephoto.
items.why: All from Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station via GSMArena. On Oct 21 he said the latest engineering sample tests a 200MP 1/1.2-inch telephoto sensor, larger than the X300 Ultra's 1/1.4-inch. GSMArena's two write-ups disagree on the battery (about 7,000mAh on Oct 19, about 8,000mAh on Oct 21), and engineering samples often change. The chip choice is the expected default for a 2027 Ultra; vivo has not announced the phone. On Oct 23 he added that the engineering sample's 35mm main camera uses a 50MP Sony LYT910 sensor (down from 200MP on the X300 Ultra, though with larger pixels). Separately, a global model (V2660) and a Brazil 'Jovi' model appeared in an IMEI database, which supports a launch outside China but says nothing about specs.

items.title: Apple plans a bigger HomeView with a 9-inch screen on a robotic arm
items.claim: Apple is developing a higher-end HomeView smart home hub with a 9-inch screen that swivels 360 degrees on a robotic arm, for 2027 or 2028.
items.why: Reported by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who has a strong Apple record, in his Oct 18 newsletter. Names like 'HomeView Max' are his guesses. The timeline is far out and Apple's plans could change; the current 7-inch HomeView ships Nov 13.

items.title: Galaxy S27 and S27+ start with just 8GB of RAM
items.claim: Because of soaring memory prices, Samsung will sell 8GB/256GB versions of the Galaxy S27 and S27+ alongside 12GB/512GB models, while the S27 Pro and Ultra start at 12GB.
items.why: From leaker @kro_roe on X, relayed by SamMobile and 9to5Google. It contradicts a September leak that had the S27 keeping the S26's 12GB base, but it fits the memory shortage: Yonhap reports most of Samsung's 2027 DRAM output is already sold to big tech customers. The same leaker says Samsung may mix UFS storage generations and cut pre-order storage upgrades. Samsung has said nothing.

items.title: Samsung launches six foldables in 2027, including a rollable Galaxy Z Slide
items.claim: Samsung's 2027 line-up will have six Galaxy Z devices: Z Flip9, Z Fold9, Z Fold9 Pro, Z Fold9 Ultra, Z TriFold2 and a rollable Z Slide, with the TriFold 2 arriving first.
items.why: From tipster @TheGalox_ on X, relayed by 9to5Google and Android Authority. Four of the names match an earlier report; the Fold9 Pro and Z Slide are new and uncorroborated. Samsung Display has shown slidable screens, but earlier reports pointed to a rollable phone in the first half of 2028, so the Slide's 2027 timing is the weakest part.

items.title: AMD's 'Gainsborough' APU powers the Steam Deck 2
items.claim: An AMD engineering sample codenamed Gainsborough, with six Zen 6-family cores and 24GB of LPDDR5-9600 in testing, is the chip for Valve's Steam Deck 2.
items.why: The benchmark listing on OpenBenchmarking is real, and kernel data places it in AMD's Zen 6 range. The Steam Deck link rests only on the codename: Gainsborough is Aerith's surname in Final Fantasy VII, and Valve's earlier Deck chips were named Aerith and Sephiroth. Its early GPU score is only slightly above the current Deck, Valve has not announced a Steam Deck 2, and TechPowerUp notes the chip could end up in other handhelds.

items.title: Huawei Mate X8 foldable launches in November
items.claim: Huawei will launch the Mate X8 in China in November with Kirin 9050/9050 Pro chips, an 8.15-inch inner and 6.5-inch cover screen, a 50MP 1/1.28-inch variable-aperture main camera, a 50MP periscope and a battery above 6,000mAh, plus a privacy-display version.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Bai Ze Guan Shan, relayed by Gizmochina and GSMArena. The timing fits Huawei's pattern (the Mate X7 launched in November 2025), but the tipster says the launch was planned alongside a new sub-brand whose timing is uncertain. Huawei has not announced anything.

items.title: Exynos Galaxy S27 models get a more efficient M2700 modem
items.claim: Exynos versions of the Galaxy S27 will use a new 4nm Samsung M2700 modem with Release 18 support, better satellite connectivity and idle power use on par with rivals; the Galaxy S28 follows with a 2nm M2800.
items.why: Reported by Korean outlet The Elec from an unnamed source, relayed by Android Authority and SamMobile. The Elec has a decent supply-chain record, but no performance figures were given and Samsung has not commented.

items.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro and Pro Max cost EUR 1,449-1,849 in Europe with smaller batteries
items.claim: The European Xiaomi 18 Pro will cost EUR 1,449 (256GB) or EUR 1,649 (512GB) with a 6,000mAh-rated battery and 90W charging, and the 18 Pro Max EUR 1,849 (512GB) with a 7,050mAh-rated battery and 100W, both smaller than the Chinese versions' 7,000mAh and 8,500mAh.
items.why: Prices first came from a single unnamed report relayed by GSMArena, and the battery figures matched Xiaomi's published EU energy labels. Update Oct 26: Italian retailer Epto listed both phones with the same smaller batteries (6,000mAh/90W on the Pro, 7,050mAh/100W on the Pro Max) and prices close to the leak: EUR 1,398.90 and 1,591.90 for the 18 Pro (256GB/512GB) and EUR 1,783.90 for the 18 Pro Max, about EUR 50-65 under the leaked figures. Epto's prices are often slightly off the official ones, so we move this to Likely: the batteries look settled, the price range is roughly right, but the exact euro figures and launch date still await Xiaomi.

items.title: Qualcomm launches two flagship Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips
items.claim: Qualcomm will unveil two Gen 6 flagship chips at Snapdragon Summit rather than one.
items.why: Qualcomm teased 'Dual 8 Elites' on Aug 19 and announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 on Sep 22. One detail was off: leaks called the second chip 'Pro', but Qualcomm named it 'Extreme'.
items.outcome: Confirmed, with a different name than leaked.

items.title: Pixel 11 prices go up $100
items.claim: Google's Pixel 11 would start at $899 and the Pro at $1,099, about $100 more than last year, after leaks of higher European prices.
items.why: Ars Technica extrapolated from European leaks; Google then priced the Pixel 11, Pro and Pro XL at $899, $1,099 and $1,299 on Aug 12.

items.title: NVIDIA has stopped making the RTX 5090
items.claim: NVIDIA has halted production of the GeForce RTX 5090 and is redirecting the GB202 chip to its professional RTX Pro cards.
items.why: Real signs pointed that way: Micro Center reclassified the card 'Not Carried', many stores sold out, and NVIDIA pulled it from its own marketplace. But on Oct 16 NVIDIA's head of personal computing, Jeff Fisher, told reporters in Taipei the RTX 5090 is not end-of-life and NVIDIA will keep shipping it, while admitting supply is tight. By Oct 17 the card was listed again on NVIDIA's US store, though not in stock.
items.outcome: Debunked by NVIDIA: the RTX 5090 has not been discontinued, though it remains scarce and expensive.

items.title: iPhone Duo 2 gets under-display Face ID
items.claim: Apple's second-generation iPhone Duo, expected next fall, adds Face ID under the outer display, and Apple is also considering an Action button.
items.why: From Bloomberg's Mark Gurman on his Power On podcast, relayed by MacRumors and 9to5Mac. Gurman has a strong Apple record, but he says Apple is only testing Face ID on prototypes and has not decided whether it will ship, so this stays a Rumor. The first iPhone Duo uses Touch ID in the side button. Early iPhone Duo reviews criticized the Touch ID placement, which makes Face ID a likely priority, but there is still no second source beyond Gurman.

items.title: Huawei adds a Pura 90 Plus with a 1-inch variable-aperture camera
items.claim: Huawei is preparing a Pura 90 Plus with a 50MP 1-inch-type RYYB variable-aperture main camera in a triple setup, a 6.8-inch 1.5K screen and four colors.
items.why: The phone itself is now official: on Oct 23 Huawei opened Pura 90 Plus pre-orders in China for an Oct 28 sale and showed four colors (matching the tipster's 'four colors') and up to 12GB/1TB. The camera and screen specs still come only from Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, who has a decent record on Chinese phones, and Huawei has not published them. On Oct 25 live images of store display units showed a 2848x1276 (1.5K-class) screen and the Kirin 9025, matching the tipster's screen claim; the 1-inch variable-aperture camera is still unconfirmed. We will resolve this on Oct 28.

items.title: Samsung's China-only W27 is a premium Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra
items.claim: Samsung will release a W27 in China, a more premium Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra in blue with gold accents.
items.why: Samsung has now confirmed on Weibo a China launch on Oct 29 for a gold-framed book-style foldable, and its linked page mentions 'W2026' and the W series. That makes a W-series Fold 8 Ultra variant very likely, but Samsung has not used the W27 name or confirmed specs; Ice Universe says it matches the Z Fold 8 Ultra. We will resolve this on Oct 29.

items.title: Apple weighs a future iPhone Duo with a roughly 8-inch inner screen
items.claim: Apple is looking at a future iPhone Duo whose inner display is about half an inch larger (roughly 7.9 to 8.1 inches, versus 7.6 today), replacing rather than joining the current size.
items.why: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said on his Power On podcast that he 'heard' Apple is 'looking at' the idea; he did not know the exact size and said it would not be a separate 'Max' model. Gurman's Apple record is strong, but this is an idea under consideration, not a product decision, so it could easily never ship.

items.title: Valve is working on a new Half-Life game codenamed 'HLX'
items.claim: 'HLX', a codename first found in 2024 game files, is an active Valve project, widely assumed to be a new Half-Life game.
items.why: On Oct 22 Valve composer Mike Morasky mentioned 'HLX has its own version' of Valve's audio HDR system during a GameSoundCon panel, and a co-panelist's reaction suggested it was a slip. That is the first time a Valve employee has said the name publicly, so the project likely exists, but nothing confirms it is a game, let alone Half-Life 3, or when it might be announced. Half-Life rumors have a long record of not panning out.

items.title: Honor 700 series launches in November with three models and a rear screen on the Pro
items.claim: Honor will launch three Honor 700 models in China in November; the 700 Pro has a 6.57-inch 1.5K screen, a 200MP main camera, a 50MP periscope telephoto, a 1.72-inch built-in rear display and a battery of about 9,000mAh.
items.why: From Weibo tipsters relayed by GSMArena: one says the event is next month and the series has three models; Digital Chat Station has repeated the 200MP camera and rear screen since August. The timing fits Honor's six-month number-series cadence (the 600 launched in May), but Honor has announced nothing. On Oct 24 Digital Chat Station added details he says come from an engineering prototype (codename 'Flora'): a roughly 9,000mAh battery, a 50MP periscope on the Pro and four test colors, while calling the November timing tentative. More detail from the same tipster, so it stays a Rumor.

items.title: vivo S70 launches soon with a 64MP periscope that supports a teleconverter
items.claim: vivo's next S-series phone, the S70, has a 64MP Sony LYT610 periscope telephoto with teleconverter support, a 6.59-inch 1.5K LTPS OLED screen and a Snapdragon 8s-series chip.
items.why: From tipster Digital Chat Station on Weibo, relayed by GSMArena; he says it is based on an engineering sample and that vivo tested, then dropped, a rear screen. DCS has a good record on Chinese phones, but this is a single source and vivo has said nothing. The S60 launched in May, so a late-2026 successor fits vivo's cadence.

items.title: Realme 17 Pro series gets a 10,000mAh battery, 200MP camera and 3.5x telephoto
items.expected: Unknown (the 16 Pro series launched in January)
items.claim: An upcoming Realme 17 Pro or 17 Pro+ has a flat 1.5K 120Hz OLED (165Hz in some games), the Dimensity 7500, a 200MP main camera, a 50MP 3.5x telephoto, a 10,000mAh battery and a plastic frame.
items.why: From a single tipster on X, relayed by GSMArena, which notes it is unclear whether this is the Pro or the Pro+. Realme has announced nothing; the leak is plausible given rivals' move to 10,000mAh batteries, but unverified.

items.title: OpenAI releases a cheaper GPT-6.1 Terra model that beats GPT-6.1 Sol
items.claim: OpenAI is about to release GPT-6.1 Terra, a new model in its Terra tier that outperforms GPT-6.1 Sol while costing less.
items.why: Two separate signals: a Microsoft pull request switched 18 evaluation configs from GPT-5.6 Terra to GPT-6.1 Terra, and The Information reported a new Terra model is coming. The model's existence is well supported, but the 'better than Sol for less' part comes only from The Information's paywalled report, and its reporter said some launches may slip into November. OpenAI has said nothing. Update Oct 26-27: OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Terra on Oct 26. It is available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users and in the API as gpt-6.1-terra at $1 per million input and $5 per million output tokens, 50% below GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI pitches it on computer use, saying it is over three times faster than Sol and GPT-6 Astra on its task benchmark, nearly matches them on MMMU-Pro and surpasses Sol on Terminal-Bench-Science, but recommends Sol or Astra for the most complex coding.
items.outcome: Mostly true. OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on Oct 26 in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API at half the API price of GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI's own benchmarks show it beating Sol on some tests (Terminal-Bench-Science) and nearly matching it on others, but OpenAI says Sol remains the better pick for the hardest coding work, so 'beats Sol' was only partly right.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, the successor to Argon, within weeks
items.claim: Google's next Gemini 4 checkpoint, Carbon, is in partner early access and will be released publicly soon.
items.why: Business Insider first reported Carbon inside Google's internal coding tool, The Information said it is coming this month, testers report it on LMArena under Google's early access program, and Carbon 'teamfood' model IDs showed up in a Google server archive. That is strong evidence it exists and is close, but Google has not announced it and the date could slip into November. Early testers say it is better than Argon at 3D work but much slower.

items.title: Xbox turns Game Pass into a pick-your-features subscription
items.claim: Microsoft will overhaul Game Pass into a tiered base plan with à la carte add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming and multiplayer.
items.why: Reported by Fortune from people familiar with the plans and relayed by GameSpot, Engadget and others. It fits an April report of a 'pick-your-own' Game Pass and CEO Asha Sharma's public goal of a 'more flexible system', but there is no timing, pricing or official confirmation, and the same Fortune story's other claims (the $1,200-1,800 next Xbox) are tracked separately.

items.title: Samsung readies a Galaxy Fit 4 that looks just like the Fit 3
items.claim: Samsung will launch a Galaxy Fit 4 (SM-R391) fitness band with a near-identical design to the Fit 3, in black, white and light blue, at a similar low price.
items.why: Android Authority obtained 360-degree videos of the band in three colors and earlier found Samsung documents naming SM-R391 as 'FIT4'; a Samsung app teardown also showed renders. The hardware is well evidenced, but specs beyond Bluetooth LE and a Goodix optical sensor, the price (the Fit 3 was about $60) and the launch date are unknown; reports range from late 2026 to early 2027.

items.title: Samsung's Exynos 2700 beats Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 phones in internal tests
items.claim: In Samsung's internal tests the Exynos 2700 for the Galaxy S27 beat the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6) by about 20% in Geekbench 6.5 multi-core and posted 5-20% higher GPU results.
items.why: A single report from Korea's Chosun Biz, relayed by Android Authority. It covers only multi-core CPU and unnamed peak GPU tests against one Xiaomi phone, with nothing on single-core speed, sustained performance, heat or battery life, and the numbers come from Samsung's own testing. A 10-core Exynos winning multi-core against an 8-core chip is plausible, but the headline 'beats Snapdragon' needs independent benchmarks.

items.title: Samsung cuts Galaxy A phone production by about 20% to protect flagships
items.claim: Samsung has cut fourth-quarter Galaxy A component orders by about 20% versus its plan, about 10 million phones a year, and plans to cut Galaxy A output by more than 10% again in 2027, shifting resources to flagships as memory costs soar.
items.why: Reported by Korea's ETNews and relayed by 9to5Google; Samsung has not commented. It fits the wider memory-price squeeze: ETNews says memory and chips now make up about half of a mid-range phone's cost and that Samsung's mobile division is losing money this year. But it rests on one outlet's supply-chain sourcing, and production plans are hard to verify from outside.

items.title: BYD's Yangwang Altior luxury sedan debuts in Dubai around Nov 5 with solid-state batteries
items.claim: BYD will unveil its 5.5-meter Yangwang Altior executive sedan in Dubai around Nov 5, as the first car with BYD's solid-state batteries, priced around 2 million yuan.
items.why: The name is official: on Oct 27 BYD revealed the sedan as the Yangwang Altior (DingYao in China) with a teaser, and Yangwang's Hu Xiaoqing had already said the global launch will be in the UAE. The Nov 5 date comes from CarNewsChina citing people familiar with the project; BYD has not announced a date. The solid-state battery and the roughly 2 million yuan price are reports only, and BYD's Stella Li has said its first solid-state car debuts in 2027, so that part is the weakest. Rear-hinged coach doors are visible in teasers and prototype photos.

items.title: Oppo Find X10 Ultra gets a LOFIC 200MP main camera, two periscopes and a 100MP selfie camera
items.claim: The Find X10 Ultra will have a 200MP 1/1.12-inch main camera with LOFIC, a 200MP periscope, a 50MP 10x periscope and a 100MP square-sensor selfie camera.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, who has a decent record on Oppo, relayed by GSMArena. By the leak's own account two sensors (the 200MP periscope and the 10x periscope) are not finalized, and the 10x camera could fall back to a smaller 1/2.76-inch sensor if the preferred 1/1.95-inch part is delayed. The phone is months away and Oppo has said nothing.

items.title: Motorola Edge 70 Neo has a Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, 7,000mAh battery and 144Hz screen
items.claim: The Edge 70 Neo will have a 6.78-inch 144Hz AMOLED, Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, 50MP Sony LYTIA 710 main camera, 32MP selfie camera, 7,000mAh battery with 45W charging and IP64.
items.why: The phone itself is real: Motorola accidentally teased it in August and renders followed. The spec list comes from a single leak reported by GSMArena with no certification or official backing yet. Motorola has not announced a launch date.

items.title: Bloober Team's Silent Hill remake targets a 2027 release
items.claim: Bloober Team's remake of the first Silent Hill, cast under the codename 'Project Noise', is aiming for a 2027 release.
items.why: Konami announced the remake in mid-2025, about eight months after Bloober's well-received Silent Hill 2 remake, but has given no date. The 2027 window and the first two cast names come from a single MP1st report, which VGC and IGN have relayed; MP1st itself says it is an internal target that can move.

items.title: iPhone 18e keeps a 60Hz screen but gets the A20 and possibly a 24MP selfie camera
items.claim: The iPhone 18e will have a 6.12-inch 60Hz LTPS OLED screen, the 2nm A20 chip, a single 48MP rear camera and maybe a 24MP front camera.
items.why: From Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, relayed by MacRumors and Android Authority. The 60Hz display repeats this leaker's earlier claim and fits Apple's pattern for the 16e and 17e, and the A20 matches what is expected for the standard iPhone 18. The leaker hedged on the front camera, and MacRumors notes 24MP may be a mix-up with the 18MP Center Stage camera. Apple has not announced the phone.
